# System-of-systems resilience engineering

**Prerequisite:** Load `.github/skills/power-ev-thermal-research/SKILL.md` and its current authority/gates before using this module.

## Trigger and objective
Activate only after a credible thermal mechanism/state/capability trajectory exists and measurable electricity/mobility service requirements have been defined.

## Steps
1. Define operator/user-grounded required service thresholds and time horizon; distinguish power supply available, actual delivered charging energy, EV/fleet readiness and mobility function.
2. Map thermal states to verified capability restrictions, then to time-dependent service; measure onset, propagation delay, degradation duration, unmet electric/charging/mobility requirement and restoration. Avoid assuming charger energy automatically equals fulfilled mobility service.
3. Construct scenario/comparator matrix: no heat, observed/credible heat, uncoupled, candidate coupling, feasible control; hold all unrelated assumptions fixed.
4. Evaluate candidate actions only when thermal response and operational constraints are supported. Characterize viability region only with qualified thresholds, states, controls, model and horizon; otherwise label exploratory.
5. Downstream sustainability is limited to the two frozen pathways: (i) interdependency→service→environmental/economic/social consequences; (ii) engineering response→changed state/capability/service→consequences. Use documented functional units and exact SDG indicator mappings, not rhetorical alignment.

## Outputs and gate
`service_register.csv`, state-time resilience metrics and comparator plots with assumptions and UQ; unsupported service thresholds and full coupled-field results remain OPEN. No new fourth research objective or broad optimization agenda.

### ECE6378 / RPG Lab overlay (S8)
L20/22 (tentative) provide supporting grid-operations/time-scale context, and the DDCP example illustrates electrical violation triggers and planning tradeoffs. Neither proves extreme-heat thermal service degradation. Activate system-of-systems resilience only after observed or appropriately qualified modeled thermal transition→capability restriction→delivered electricity/mobility service. Distinguish EV adoption threshold from thermal activation and do not silently extend the thesis into general BESS planning/SCUC or universal electricity resilience.
